subject: Inference execution locations and export-control considerations
messages:
From: Oliver Smith <oliver@skyohealth.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Quick Q — do EU user requests ever leave EEA?

Hi Evelyn,

We’re doing our final privacy & export-control pass ahead of a pilot and Legal had two quick questions:

1) For inference calls originating from EU users, can you confirm whether any model execution artifacts (model weights, activations, KV cache, or logs) are ever routed outside the EEA by default?
2) Which subprocessors (compute, storage, monitoring) you rely on for EU processing, and whether any of those have US-based dependencies that would cause cross-border exports?

If you have a short one-pager or inventory we can share with our compliance team that’d be perfect.

Thanks — can we aim to have this by EOD Thursday so we can signoff?

—Oliver
Senior Product Manager, Skyo Health

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Quick Q — do EU user requests ever leave EEA?

Hi Oliver,

Thanks for the clear questions — happy to clarify. Short answers up-front:

- Default behavior: Inference requests from EU users are routed to EU execution zones (we map by origin IP / customer routing policies). Runtime artifacts needed for the request (ephemeral activations and KV cache) are kept in-region and are not written out-of-region by default.
- Persistent artifacts: Model binaries (weights) for the EU-hosted model replica remain on EU-resident block storage unless you choose a global model variant.
- Subprocessors: We use a mix of EU-based compute partners + EU buckets for durable telemetry; we do use a global monitoring provider that may have US-based processing for aggregated telemetry, but we can filter or suppress identifiable inference tokens for pilot customers.

I’m looping in Rishi (technical) and Monica (security/compliance) to add details and provide the inventory pack. We’ll attach a short residency map and our current subprocessor inventory.

Would you prefer a redacted inventory (no IPs) or the full CSV for legal review?

Best,
Evelyn
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Quick Q — do EU user requests ever leave EEA? (technical detail)

Hi Oliver — quick technical breakdown from runtime/hosting side (keeps to the questions asked):

1) Request routing and execution
- Our edge routing maps requests to the nearest configured execution zone by default. For EU-origin traffic we route to eu-west-1 / West Europe zones (customer can pin to region in the Dedicated/Private product).
- Model execution (transformer forward pass) and ephemeral KV/activation buffers are allocated on GPUs in-region. KV cache is held in-memory for the duration of the session and flushed; we do not persist per-request KV caches to multi-region storage.

2) Persistent storage and model binaries
- If you select our EU-hosted model SKU, the model weights are stored on EU-block storage and snapshots remain in-region. For cross-region model promotion (global SKU) we replicate snapshots under customer consent.

3) Telemetry, logs, and monitoring
- Service-level telemetry (latency, error rates) is aggregated centrally and may traverse to our monitoring vendor which has a US processing footprint. We offer a filtered telemetry mode for customers who need only region-localized metrics (removes request-level text).

4) Subprocessors (short list relevant to EU runs)
- Compute partner: CloudForge GmbH (DE) — runs EU GPU pools and holds physical servers in DE datacenters.
- Object storage: EuroStore S.A. (NL) — EU-bucketed durable storage for model snapshots/backups.
- Monitoring: BeaconMetrics Ltd. (global) — aggregates anonymized metrics; has US backend.
- Key management: Customer-controlled KMS (recommended) or Redwood-managed KMS (HSM keys stored in EU on request).

5) Export-control / controls for outbound transfers
- We support a policy engine to enforce in-region execution and to block replication to non-EEA destinations.
- For customers in regulated sectors, we can commit to no-export clauses in the DPA and provide an evidence pack (SOC2 summary, subprocessor list, residency map).

If useful I can also provide a compact diagram of request flow (edge → execution → ephemeral cache → response) showing where data is encrypted in transit and at rest.

—Rishi
Senior Applied ML Engineer, Redwood Inference
